android.desc:
Calendar Widgets Classic – Elevate Your Scheduling on Android! A fully offline calendar tool with a range of customizable options — no internet permission, no ads. Boost your daily organization and never miss an event.

💡 Why Choose Calendar Widgets Classic?

▪  Works Everywhere: Available for all Android smartphones and tablets.
▪  Private by Design: No internet permission, so your events never leave your device. No ads, no analytics, no tracking.
▪  Sleek Design: Over 50 themes to choose from, ensuring a modern and attractive interface.
▪  User-Friendly: An intuitive dashboard designed for all ages. Perfect word-wrapping for easy readability.
▪  Versatile Viewing: Display your events by day, week, or month. Choose from numerous color themes.
▪  Compatibility: Works with Google Calendar and any other calendar already synced on your device.
▪  Customizations: Adjust the start day of your week, set default event durations, and much more!

Key features At a Glance:
▪ Multiple view options: day, week, month, and list
▪ Easy tap actions for event viewing and addition
▪ Highlights for today's events
▪ Works fully offline, with no network access
▪ Compatible with popular launchers

Organize better and smarter with Calendar Widgets Classic. Incorporate our widget on your home screen and witness improved productivity. Regardless of whether you're already using another calendar tool, our widgets complement and enhance your scheduling. Download today and step into an organized future!

quotes.text:
I'm assuming you're looking for the monthly planner view that actually shows events and not just indicators? Try calendar widgets suite or business calendar 2 planner. Unfortunately both are ad-supported (anything designed explicitly to show local personal information shouldn't go online IMHO), but there's a paid version as well. There's a couple other apps that have similar looking widgets as well, you might find more by searching for monthly planner widgets, not calendar widgets. It might also be possible to find one using a week toolkit (I used Zooper in the past, but I think it's pretty dead now; not sure what's replaced it).
